crossConcepts.reason: After the division/remainder degree constraint fixes g=-x²-x+q, the integer-root condition must be tested on the remaining quadratic factor g+1. The q=3 candidate gives x²+x−4 with nonintegral roots, whereas q=11 gives (x−3)(x+4). Quadratic roots are necessary beyond the primary division structure; merely observing the product factorization is not a separate additional concept.

integrationPattern.reason: The known root x=3 can come from either -x+q=0 or -x²-x+q+1=0. These give q=3 and q=11, and the three-distinct-integer-roots condition rejects q=3.
